concept: Labeled Property Graph vs RDF Triplestore Storage Models

claims.text: Labeled Property Graphs store attributes directly on nodes and edges with pointer-based index-free adjacency, allowing O(1) traversal per hop without index scans, whereas traditional RDF stores decompose data into Subject-Predicate-Object triples requiring multi-way index joins.

RDF engines enforce formal semantics via OWL ontologies and SHACL constraints, providing automated deductive reasoning and global URI disambiguation that standard property graph schemas lack without external validation layers.

For variable-length path traversal (k > 3), property graphs with index-free adjacency exhibit sub-linear latency growth relative to total graph size, while triple stores encounter combinatorial join-state growth unless path queries are pre-indexed or translated into transitive reachability indices.
